content: 1. Packaging instructions for certain materials, such as infectious substances, are not subject to additional requirements outlined in these regulations, provided they are prepared correctly for transport. Infectious substances may only include materials necessary to maintain their viability, stabilize them, prevent degradation, or neutralize their hazards. 2. Dangerous goods in quantities of 30 milliliters or less, classified as flammable liquids (Class 3), corrosives (Class 8), or miscellaneous dangerous substances (Class 9, including environmentally hazardous substances), may be packed in primary receptacles containing infectious substances. When these small quantities are packed with infectious substances according to the specified packing instructions, no further requirements from these regulations need to be met. 3. Approved packaging types include drums (e.g., 1A2, 1B2, 1N2, 1H2, 1D, 1G), boxes (e.g., 4A, 4B, 4N, 4C1, 4C2, 4D, 4F, 4G, 4H1, 4H2), and jerricans (e.g., 3A2, 3B2, 3H2). These packagings must meet Packing Group II performance standards for solids. 4. For larger quantities of liquids, approved packaging types include drums (e.g., 1A1, 1A2, 1B1, 1B2, 1N1, 1N2, 1H1, 1H2, 1D, 1G), jerricans (e.g., 3A1, 3A2, 3B1, 3B2, 3H1, 3H2), and composite packagings (e.g., 6HA1, 6HB2, 6HG1, 6HH1, 6HD1, 6HA2, 6HB2, 6HC, 6HD2, 6HG2, 6HH2, 6PA1, 6PB1, 6PG1, 6PD1, 6PH1, 6PH2, 6PA2, 6PB2, 6PC, 6PG2, 6PD2). These packagings must meet Packing Group II performance standards for liquids. 5. 6. For carbon dioxide (solid or dry ice), the following requirements apply: A Shipper's Declaration is required only when dry ice is used as a refrigerant for dangerous goods requiring such a declaration or when it is used for substances not subject to these regulations but described on a Shipper's Declaration. Alternative written documentation describing the contents may replace the dangerous goods transport document requirements, provided the information is clearly presented in the designated location for goods description. If an agreement exists with the operator, the shipper may provide the required information electronically via EDP (Electronic Data Processing) or EDI (Electronic Data Interchange). 7. The required information for dry ice shipments includes: UN number (UN 1845). Proper shipping name (Carbon dioxide, solid or Dry ice). The number of packages and the net quantity of dry ice in each package. The net mass of dry ice must be marked on the outside of the package. For overpacks, the total net quantity of dry ice in the overpack must be marked on the outside. 8. Dry ice used for purposes other than dangerous goods may be shipped in unit load devices or pallets prepared by a single shipper, provided: Prior arrangements are made with the operator. Marking and labeling requirements for unit load devices do not apply. The unit load device must not contain dangerous goods other than UN 3373 (Biological substance, Category B) or ID 8000 (Consumer commodity). If these substances are included, all applicable regulations must be followed in addition to the provisions outlined here. The shipper must provide the operator with written documentation or electronic information (if agreed upon) stating the total quantity of dry ice contained in the unit load device or pallet.
